sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:176906
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 39456 of 2024
Applicant :- Raghuvir

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Somit Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Siddharth Shukla, learned Advocate filed his power on behalf of the applicant along with
supplementary affidavit, today in the Court, which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Siddharth Shukla and Sri Somit Shukla, learned counsels for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 141 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Barsana,
District Mathura during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is father-in-law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter along with other family members including husband of the deceased.
Raghuvir vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131443477/
1 5.

He further submits actually deceased i.e. daughter-in-law of the applicant was short tampered lady and on the date of incident she insisted her husband to visit Ram Navmi Fair but when her husband did not take her to fair then in anger and rash she committed suicide by hanging herself.
He further submits even post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

6. He further submits, in the FIR of the present case there is no specific allegation of demand of dowry and this fact shows that on the basis of vague allegation of demand of dowry, FIR of the present case was lodged.

7. He next submits that there is no specific allegation against the applicant and applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 19.04.2024 i.e. for last more than six months.
8.
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, daughter-in-law of the applicant died within two years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is father-in-law of the deceased and there is no specific allegation against him.

11. Further, in the FIR there is no specific allegation of demand of dowry has been disclosed and as per post mortem, deceased died due to hanging, therefore, prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.

12. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 19.04.2024 i.e. for last more than six months.
13.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant - Raghuvir be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from Raghuvir vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131443477/
2
disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024 AK Pandey  Raghuvir vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131443477/
